title.narrative: Output 1.1. Increased institutional capacity of employer and business membership organizations (EBMOs)

description.narrative:
According to its Strategic Framework 2018-23, Employers Confedetaion of the Philippines (ECOP) aims to proactively engage in national policymaking. However, ECOP had been relatively weak in policy advocacy compared to its service provision. The uncertainty brought by the pandemic created a demand for ECOP to channel private sector needs to the government and participate in social dialogue mechanisms. To address this, ECOP excecuted a project “Supporting Employers and Business Capacity on Employment Generation and Policy Advocacy for Business Recovery”. ECOP conducted evidence-based research to analyse the business environment and devise strategies for fostering job creation and business recovery. It developed advocacy tools to address issues on skills mismatch, industry-academic partnerships, and training for emerging skills. ECOP delivered policy recommendations to government officials and journalists during the National Conference of Employers (NCE) in June 2023. At the NCE, a resolution was adopted, urging the government to enhance upskilling/reskilling programs, support just transition towards sustainable workplaces and provide incentives for productive business models. The government responded positively in its concluding statements. The recommendations were subsequently submitted to the government and conveyed to the media. During this process, ECOP took the lead in forming alliances with the Philippine Chamber of Commerce and Industry (PCCI) and the Philippine Exporters Confederation (PHILEXPORT). ECOP revitalized the functions of the Technical Working Group on Labour & Social Policy and the Chapter Consultative Council. ECOP convened the Leaders Forum (LF), a national bipartite dialogue mechanism, to put forth policy recommendations to the government. Through the LF, ECOP systematically and continuously engaged with the government and unions to effectively represent the views of employers in policymaking. The ILO contributed with expertise to bolster ECOP’s policy recommendations regarding job creation and sustainable business recovery. These recommendations were developed together with ECOP Secretariat, specifically its Advocacy, Research, and Communications Department. The ILO assisted ECOP secretariat in devising plans, strategies, and campaign materials, accompanied by multiple collaborative meetings to shape business recovery agendas. In particular, the ILO enhanced ECOP’s capacity in designing and conducting surveys, as well as formulating policy recommendations. For example, the ILO delivered training and coaching sessions on effectively utilizing Qualtrics (cloud-based software data platform) for survey distribution, analysis and reporting; and supported the final analysis and drafting of reports. Two rounds of Qualtrics training were conduced by the ILO for ECOP staff (May 2022 and March 2023). These training sessions equipped ECOP personnel with the skills build surveys, interpret survey results and export data, create dynamic visualizations and reports, create dashboards. This capacity building aimed to empower ECOP to independently undertake similar projects in the future. Morover, the ILO organized training workshops for ECOP. One focused on evidence-based policy making for decent work (May 2023) while another covered strategic advocacy and effective influencing (including lobbying, negotiation), communication skills for advocacy (such as writing policy position papers, developing post-position paper materials like news articles, press releases, feature writing, copywriting) and digital advocacy through social media (Oct 2023).
The ILO supported ECOP in leading bipartite social dialogue through the LF. Comprising of the largest business organizations, including ECOP, PCCI and PHILEXPORT, and the most representative trade unions in the Philippines, LF benefited from the ILO’s involvement in fostering effective social dialogue.
